chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:
If there remained on the earth only two people, one of them would be the Hujjah (or the second would be the Hujjah).

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: The Hujjah (Proof), a title for the Imam who serves as the divine proof for humanity.

ai.seo_question: Who is the Hujjah if only two people remain on earth?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the indispensability of the Imam as the 'Hujjah' (Proof of God) for the continuity of divine guidance. It emphasizes that the Imam’s presence is not merely beneficial but ontologically necessary for the validity of worship and knowledge, ensuring that God’s argument remains complete even in the most minimal human community.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid al-Barqi from Ali bin Issma’eel from Muhammad bin Sinan that Hamza bin at-Tayyar had heard Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) saying: “
If there are no people on the earth except two, one of them will be al-Hujjah.”
